claim: Flag $8D (proposed wa_arrival_cutscene_started, bit 5 of byte $0A11) is set by wa78_intro at the start of the Watermia arrival cutscene; with it set the five av69 and five av6A party actors die at spawn and the Angel Village world-map exit (scene $69, tiles (29,0D)-(2C,0F)) offers menu $0A 'Quit / Watermia' instead of menu $15 'Quit only'.

start.state: arrival scene not yet shown ($75 clear)

trial.control: load scene $69 with $8D and $75 clear; watch the five NPCs and the joypad lock; after the scene walk to tiles (29,0D)-(2C,0F)
trial.forced: write byte $0A11 |= $20 (the flag) before loading scene $69, then repeat; load scene $6A the same way
observe: bit 5 of byte $0A11
actor list of scene $69 and $6A (five party actors present or absent)
world-map menu id staged by OverworldExitAngelVillageStage ($0A or $15)
screenshot of the menu

confirms: the flag is read by exactly these consumers: the ten party actors die and the exit menu includes Watermia
refutes: any other behaviour at the exit, or party actors present with the flag set

claim: In scene $75 (Ishtar's test) the apprentice sets scratch $00 only when the scene starts with the player inside tiles (70,00)-(80,10), the fourth observation room; the player's idle, ladder and shimmy code then uses the alternate ('Shadow') sprite set, which is the 'The wind blew your hair around' difference of the last room.

start.state: enter through warp #07 of scene $75 (lands at (0798,00B0)) and through warp #05 (lands at (0598,00B0), the third room, as a control)

trial.control: load scene $75 at the corridor (Y >= $F0), open door 0, stand still in the first room and read $0A00 bit 0 and the idle sprite
trial.forced: load scene $75 directly at pixel (0798,00B0) with $0AA6 = 7; repeat at (0598,00B0)
observe: bit 0 of byte $0A00 after the apprentice's first tick
player idle sprite id (#00-#03 normal or #10-#13 alternate)
playerSpeedNs ($09B4) on the first frames
screenshot of Will standing in the room

confirms: $00 is set only in the fourth room and the idle sprite set changes there
refutes: the byte is set in other rooms, or the idle sprite does not change

claim: In scene $73 (waterfall tunnel) scratch $00 follows the player: set while the player stands in tiles (2A,17)-(2F,1D), clear elsewhere, and set at spawn (with the sound actor gone) when the player starts in tiles (00,00)-(40,10); the player code uses the alternate idle sprite set while it is set.

observe: bit 0 of byte $0A00 per frame
idle sprite id
whether APUIO0 ($2140) is written every fourth frame in the start-box case

claim: Using the Magic Dust (item #14) on Kara's picture sets scratch $01 of scene $74 and removes the item without testing $89; scratch $01 is lost on any scene load and av74_kara enters its rescue script only while the player carries item #14, so leaving scene $74 after using the dust (or using it before the test is passed) leaves the rescue unreachable.

start.state: item #14 (Magic Dust) in the inventory, standing at tiles (07,08)-(09,0A); run once with av_ishtar_riddles_solved clear and once set

trial.control: with $89 set (flag 137, byte $0A11 bit 1), use the dust at (07,08)-(09,0A), interact with the picture, watch the rescue cutscene
trial.forced: with $89 clear, use the dust, walk out through any warp of scene $74 and back in, solve the test (or set $89 directly) and interact with the picture; also: with $89 set, use the dust, leave and re-enter before interacting
observe: bit 1 of byte $0A00 (scratch $01) after each load
inventory slot of item #14
text printed by the picture's interact handler
bit 2 of byte $0A11 ($8A) and bit 4 ($8C)
screenshot of the picture handler text

confirms: the rescue is unreachable once the dust is spent without the kiss, or that another path restores it
refutes: the item or the state survives the scene reload

observe: word $0AA6 at scene $6B load, after the door opens and on entry to scene $75
which door of scene $75 responds first ('Don't hurry' versus opening)
